statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
A binary tree is height-balanced when, at every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most 1.
Return true if the tree is height-balanced, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: 6 (index 9) is the left child of 5, and 7 (index 19) is the left child of 6. Node 5 then has a left subtree of height 2 and an empty right subtree, a difference of 2.
Every level is full, so at each node the two subtrees have exactly the same height.
